observations.statement: The core separates file cleanup inside a worktree from later worktree-directory removal and fixes their lifecycle order.
Orchestrator and interview runner calls are directed through run_with_cleanup, with unit verification surrounding the iteration-level prepare, execute, and cleanup sequence.
Parallel cleanup is scoped to each subtask working directory, and post-execution cleanup is limited to runner temporary files before commit while full untracked cleanup occurs before execution.
Named PM output directories are allowlisted, and newly introduced interview or orchestrator output must remain under .puppet-master or be added to the allowlist.
Subprocess output is required to use bounded drop-oldest buffers and the CLI is required to run in a separate process; background output has a conditional preserve-or-clear policy hook.

Cleanup crews are optional overlays composed of PM child runs, use explicit shared state and crew-board messages, and do not treat hidden memory or active-agent side files as canonical coordination state.
Blocked cleanup actions expose canonical reason and allowed-action identifiers, while retry, reroute, cancellation, and continuity preserve canonical lineage and reconstruct from canonical state.

Cleanup must preserve retry baselines and live history, distinguishes storage-presence state from semantic validity, uses node-level artifact boundaries, separates lifecycle verbs, and retains safe-point and remediation lineage through terminal conditions.

Temporary debug mutation requires a restore point, instrumentation identity and scope, automatic cleanup on resolved, cancelled, or superseded investigations, a failed_cleanup state on residue, and continued user visibility of unresolved remnants.

The debug cleanup contract prohibits overlapping active instrumentation, requires residual cleanup summary data, exact env/config reversion, secret handling before evidence transfer, and truthful profiler-detach failure reporting.
MiscPlan remains the owner for preserved cleanup behavior, with storage mechanics and rewrite alignment assigned to named cross-document owners.
M-002 makes cleanup activity and retained evidence first-class event artifacts and assigns redb retention metadata and rollups.
M-003 prescribes a DRY-oriented backend implementation sequence from centralized cleanup helpers through wrapper adoption and later retention and manual-clean behavior.
M-004 is explicitly GUI-related, requires Expert and ELI5 cleanup copy selected by app Interaction Mode while keeping Chat ELI5 separate, and depends on M-003.
The three PlanUnits use source preservation, traceability, prohibition of executable task generation, and plan migration/index commands as their stated acceptance and validation surfaces.

candidate_findings.title: Runner wrapper failure semantics are undefined
candidate_findings.statement: The core fixes the normal prepare, execute, and cleanup order and prohibits raw runner execution, but it does not specify whether cleanup runs after prepare or execute failure, cancellation, or panic, nor how simultaneous execute and cleanup errors are prioritized and returned.
candidate_findings.impact: Different call sites can skip cleanup, overwrite the primary failure, or commit against partially cleaned state, undermining the promised single execution path and recovery lineage.

candidate_findings.title: Safe-point retention cutoffs use unresolved terminal language
candidate_findings.statement: Failed-run state is retained until an attempt is terminal or superseded, while the addendum retains safe-point metadata until terminal resolution and remediation metadata until the parent is terminal; the window does not define whether superseded is terminal resolution or how parent and attempt terminality interact.
candidate_findings.impact: An implementation can delete recovery state too early after supersession or retain it indefinitely because the authoritative release condition is ambiguous.

candidate_findings.title: Cleanup lifecycle states and verbs lack an executable transition contract
candidate_findings.statement: The core names retained, cleanup_eligible, archived, removed, and revoked semantics and separates recover, archive, prune, remove, and Clean all worktrees, but provides no legal transition graph, entry predicates, actor authority, concurrency guard, or idempotency rules.
candidate_findings.impact: Builders can implement incompatible or destructive state transitions while still using every required state and verb token.

candidate_findings.title: Cleanup envelopes and command ownership are not typed
candidate_findings.statement: The normalized envelope is a list of identifiers and context fields rather than a field-level schema, and native-surface ownership is required without defining the surface identifier, ownership resolution, validation, or rejection response.
candidate_findings.impact: Producers and consumers can disagree on required fields, types, correlation identity, and authorization, causing lost lineage or route and cleanup commands to act on the wrong surface.

candidate_findings.title: A lifecycle requirement is an orphaned sentence fragment
candidate_findings.statement: The statement that something persists at cleanup operations has no subject, scope, or state name, while the recoverable-error remediation loop has no trigger or owner in the sentence.
candidate_findings.impact: The intended persisted object and remediation obligation cannot be implemented or tested deterministically from this text.

candidate_findings.title: Restore-point sufficiency has no pre-mutation oracle
candidate_findings.statement: The core requires a restore point sufficient to revert temporary debug state and requires collector lifecycle and rollback declarations, but it gives no validation evidence, minimum captured state, atomicity rule, or abort behavior when restore-point creation or validation fails.
candidate_findings.impact: Invasive instrumentation can begin with an unusable restore point, leaving code, tooling, remote-host, or configuration residue that cannot be safely reverted.

candidate_findings.title: Instrumentation overlap exclusion is race-prone
candidate_findings.statement: The prohibition on two active investigations adding overlapping instrumentation does not define target identity, overlap, lock granularity, atomic acquisition, stale-owner recovery, or which investigation wins a race.
candidate_findings.impact: Concurrent investigations can mutate the same target and later remove or misattribute each other's instrumentation and evidence.

candidate_findings.title: Secret evidence sanitization is non-deterministic
candidate_findings.statement: The requirement permits either redaction or hashing and uses open-ended categories such as obvious secrets and other IDs without defining detection rules, hashing parameters, replacement format, false-negative handling, or a verification oracle.
candidate_findings.impact: Sensitive values can survive storage or export, while inconsistent sanitization can also destroy correlation evidence needed for audit and recovery.

candidate_findings.title: Cleanup GUI copy selection lacks fallback and accessibility behavior
candidate_findings.statement: M-004 requires Expert and ELI5 variants and Interaction Mode selection, but the window does not provide the copy contract, missing-variant fallback, mode-change timing, localization behavior, or accessibility requirements for tooltip, help, and discoverability content.
candidate_findings.impact: Implementations can expose inconsistent or inaccessible cleanup explanations and can disagree about when the displayed variant changes.

candidate_findings.title: PlanUnit validation does not name behavioral acceptance oracles
candidate_findings.statement: M-002, M-003, and M-004 state runtime, architecture, implementation-order, and GUI obligations, but their listed acceptance and validation surfaces cover exact-text preservation, traceability, non-generation of executable tasks, plan migration validation, and plan index validation rather than named runtime or GUI behavior checks.
candidate_findings.impact: The PlanUnits can satisfy their stated gates without evidence that cleanup events, wrapper adoption, retention behavior, or Interaction Mode copy selection actually behave as specified.

candidate_findings.title: Background-output retention has no default policy
candidate_findings.statement: The background-output clause conditionally says output should be preserved or cleared per policy but does not state a default, retention duration, clearing trigger, user override, or behavior when the policy is absent.
candidate_findings.impact: Agent output may be deleted unexpectedly or retained without bound across implementations.

candidate_findings.title: Failed-cleanup recovery exits are unspecified
candidate_findings.statement: The debug lifecycle defines failed_cleanup, a cleanup-failed stop reason, residual summaries, and user-visible residue, but does not define retry eligibility, allowed transitions out of failed_cleanup, who may accept follow-up residue, or when cleanup ownership is released.
candidate_findings.impact: Investigations can become permanently stuck, silently relinquish residue, or race with later investigations despite emitting the required failure state.

explicit_non_gaps.statement: The window explicitly distinguishes cleanup of files inside a worktree from removal of the worktree directory and orders both operations.
The window explicitly establishes a shared runner wrapper, rejects direct runner.execute calls in new orchestrator code, and places prepare and cleanup inside unit verification boundaries.
Parallel-worktree cleanup scope and the separation between pre-run untracked cleaning and post-run temporary-file cleaning are explicit.
Named .puppet-master outputs and the rule for allowlisting future output paths are explicit.
Bounded subprocess output and separate-process CLI execution are explicit cross-plan constraints.
Cleanup crew actor identity and canonical coordination-state boundaries are explicit.
Blocked-action identifiers and lineage preservation across retry, reroute, cancellation, and handoff reconstruction are explicit.
The window explicitly forbids erasing retry baselines, live lineage, and canonical recovery history and makes tier-era files compatibility inputs rather than canonical scope anchors.
Automatic cleanup terminal triggers, failed_cleanup reporting, visible unresolved residue, and the prohibition on claiming profiler cleanup success after detach failure are explicit.
Exact reversion of temporary env or config activation is explicit.
MiscPlan ownership and named storage and rewrite boundary ownership are explicit.
M-004's GUI classification and dependency on M-003 are explicit.

unknowns.statement: The stage-by-stage error, cancellation, panic, and error-precedence behavior of run_with_cleanup is not stated in the assigned window.
Whether superseded is a terminal resolution for safe-point release, and whether child-attempt or parent-lineage terminality controls deletion, is not stated.
The allowed values, types, and producer of blocked_reason_code and allowed_action_ids are not enumerated in this window.
The requiredness, types, versioning, and validation rules for normalized cleanup/run envelope fields are not stated.
The transition table, authorization, and idempotency semantics for cleanup states and lifecycle verbs are not stated.
Whether background agents are implemented and which preserve-or-clear policy applies when no explicit setting exists are not stated.
M-002 does not state retention durations, authoritative timestamps, rollup algorithms, or deletion eligibility for redb retention metadata.
The definition of an instrumentation target and overlap, and the mechanism that atomically excludes competing investigations, are not stated.
The secret detector, redaction format, hash algorithm, and sanitization acceptance test are not stated.
The concrete Expert and ELI5 strings, fallback behavior, localization, mode-switch timing, and accessibility semantics are not stated.
The subject of the phrase that persists at cleanup operations is unknowable from the sentence fragment.
The window does not state that the named plan migration and index validators execute any cleanup runtime or GUI behavior.

exact_evidence_refs.exact_quote: Worktree plan's "cleanup" is **removing the worktree directory** after merge (`cleanup_subtask_worktree`, `remove_worktree`). MiscPlan's cleanup is **removing untracked/ignored files *inside* ** the workspace or worktree. Both apply: after an iteration, run MiscPlan's cleanup_after_execution in that worktree; when the subtask is done and merged, run Worktree's remove_worktree.
All agent runs (main iteration and subagent runs) should go through the same prepare → execute → cleanup flow.
Do not call `runner.execute()` directly from new orchestrator/subagent code; use the wrapper from MiscPlan §4.6.
So the flow is: verify_tier_start (unit) -> ... -> prepare_working_directory (iteration) -> execute -> cleanup_after_execution (iteration) -> ... -> verify_tier_end (unit).
Each parallel subtask has its own worktree and working_dir. cleanup_after_execution runs in that subtask's work_dir only (per MiscPlan §3.3).
So cleanup_after_execution must not remove untracked files (§9.1.13); only runner temp files. Full workspace untracked clean runs in prepare_working_directory (before the run).
that call must go through **run_with_cleanup** so the interview working directory is prepared and cleaned the same way as orchestrator and start_chain.

All are under `.puppet-master/` and thus allowlisted. When adding new output paths in the interview or orchestrator plans, keep them under `.puppet-master/` or add them to the cleanup allowlist so they are never removed (§9.1.14).

**Plans/newfeatures.md §13** (Bounded buffers and process isolation) requires that all subprocess output (runners, headless, stream consumers) use **bounded buffers** (fixed max size, drop oldest when full) and that the CLI always runs in a **separate process**.

**§2** (Background/async agents) defines output for background runs at `.puppet-master/agent-output/{run-id}/`; if that feature is implemented, the cleanup allowlist and optional "agent output" policy (§3.2, §5) should account for that path so background run output is preserved or cleared per policy.
cleanup crews are optional overlays, not a separate persistent actor system.
cleanup crew members remain PM child runs.
crew coordination uses explicit shared state and crew-board messages when enabled.
hidden memory files and active-agent side files are not canonical cleanup coordination state.
blocked cleanup actions use canonical `blocked_reason_code` and `allowed_action_ids[]`.
cleanup retries, reroutes, and cancellation preserve canonical lineage.
cleanup continuity comes from canonical state and handoff reconstruction, not child-memory files.
persists at cleanup operations; remediation loop runs when cleanup operations fail with recoverable errors.
prepare/cleanup logic must not erase or invalidate the baseline needed for `retry_from_safe_point`
cleanup after failed runs must preserve enough state for scheduler/runtime recovery until the attempt is terminal or superseded

`Plans/MiscPlan.md` / `/MiscPlan.md` cleanup states distinguish retained, cleanup_eligible, archived, and removed lane or `/worktree` states; `removed` is a backing-object or storage-presence state, while `revoked` is semantic validity state.

Normalized cleanup/run envelopes include `CLI_Bridged_Providers`, `CLI_Bridged_Providers.md`, `{ run_id, seq, type, payload }`, run_id, thread_id, attempt_id, node_id, snapshot IDs, remediation lineage, `/node/attempt/lineage`, `/event`, `/trust`, rewrite-era correlation, actor kind, effective account, switch reason, lane/worktree identity, and pressure/trust context.
Live cleanup must never erase run, lane, or worktree lineage from `History`, `Ledger`, graph-linked inspection, or `/lane/worktree` records.

Cleanup artifact boundaries are node-level, not tier-scoped; tier-era state file names such as `progress.txt`, `AGENTS.md`, and `prd.json` are compatibility inputs for `/cleanup`, not canonical scoping anchors.
Lane lifecycle verbs are separate: recover, archive, prune, remove, and `Clean all worktrees` must not blur together, and cleanup actions may expose prune or recover without implying remove.
Cleanup command payloads with generic `page: string` or tier-bound filters must be constrained with native-surface ownership so they cannot undermine route/open or cleanup commands.
keep safe-point metadata until the originating attempt lineage reaches terminal resolution
keep remediation lineage metadata until the parent lineage is terminal
cleanup may compact derived summaries, but must not destroy the canonical history needed for recovery explanation and audit

before invasive instrumentation or temporary dependency/tooling changes, PM creates or updates a restore point backed by `runtime_artifact.restore_point` that is sufficient to revert the investigation's temporary state if cleanup fails
every temporary debug mutation lane carries an `instrumentation_id`, declared scope, and explicit cleanup obligation
resolved, cancelled, and superseded investigations attempt cleanup automatically; failed cleanup transitions the investigation to `failed_cleanup` instead of pretending success
unresolved instrumentation remnants must remain user-visible until cleaned up or explicitly accepted as follow-up work

Any temporary-instrumentation patch pipeline must declare an `instrumentation_id`, `collector_state` (`collector-state` in source-lineage/audit vocabulary), collector lifecycle transitions, the install/collect/remove sequence, debug-specific mutation rules, the evidence sink contract, and explicit write `/cleanup/rollback` semantics.
Auto-cleanup is mandatory for resolved, cancelled, and superseded investigations; failed residue uses lifecycle `failed_cleanup` with `stop_reason_code = investigation.cleanup_failed`.
PM must not let two active investigations add overlapping temporary instrumentation to the same target.
A bundle-record must carry the cleanup_summary, including cleanup_summary.residual_items[] / residual_items, stop_reason_code, and any surviving residue.
Env/config activation cleanup must revert the exact temporary flag `/toggle/value` PM introduced.

Secret evidence handling must redact/hash obvious secrets `/tokens`, including `Authorization`, cookies, session IDs, API keys, passwords, private tokens, and other IDs before storage, export, or bundle handoff.

Debugger `/profiler` attach instrumentation must detach the temporary attach/profiler `/session`; if detach fails but no durable workspace mutation remains, keep the failure localized to runtime/session state and do not claim cleanup success.

During this batch, `Plans/MiscPlan.md` remains the owner doc for the behavior described by its preserved sections, while cross-doc ownership follows the ContractRefs and boundary notes already present in the original text.

canonical_text: Cleanup actions, retained artifacts, evidence, and manual Clean workspace activity are first-class artifacts/events in the unified event model, with redb carrying retention policy, retention metadata, and rollups while cleanup boundaries align to patch/apply/verify/rollback rather than UI-only affordances.
